outcome.label: Outcome:
outcome.sentNote: <mono>sent</mono> means the mail server accepted the message, not necessarily that it reached the inbox. The system cannot see messages that land in spam or are blocked on the receiving side.
outcome.unknownNote: It is unclear whether the message went out — the mail server did not respond in time. The system does not resend automatically, so the recipient never gets it twice. To resend, the app service sends a new request.
outcome.recipientGone: no longer in the recipient list
outcome.whyBlocked: To see why this person was blocked: open <link>the page of <mono>{id}</mono></link>. Settings there are current, not as of sending.

overview.alertFailed: {count} failed sends in the last 24 hours.
overview.alertQueue: The queue is long: {waiting} messages, the oldest waiting since {oldest}. The send rate is a shared limit of the sending mailbox, split across all apps.

overview.alertUnusable: {unusable}/{total} recipients have no usable email (not set {missing} · unsubscribed {unsubscribed} · broken address {invalid}).

notifications.noRecipientTip: Not sent because the recipient is blocked. This is the system working as intended, not an error.
notifications.emptyLoosen: Loosen the status or topic filter.

notifications.emptyRecipientFiltered: No email to «{id}» matches the filters. The ID must match exactly, character by character.

notifications.scheduledSubtitle: Sends waiting for their run time — content is locked

errorCodes.byCodeTitle: Read errors by <mono>code</mono>, not by wording
errorCodes.byCodeBody: Every error is <mono>application/problem+json</mono>. For <mono>422</mono>, the outer <mono>code</mono> is just <mono>VALIDATION</mono> — the specific code is in <mono>issues[].code</mono>, with <mono>path</mono> pointing to the wrong field.
errorCodes.retryBody: <mono>4xx</mono>: do not retry unchanged — it will fail the same way. <mono>5xx</mono> and timeouts: retry with backoff, keeping the same <mono>idempotencyKey</mono> field in the body — the same key never sends twice. The MVP does not return <mono>429</mono> yet.
errorCodes.acceptedBody: The email goes out later, from the queue. Track it with <mono>GET /v1/notifications/:id</mono>. Even <mono>sent</mono> only means the mail server accepted it, not necessarily that it reached the inbox.

lifecycle.horizon: Point of no return — first batch left the queue
lifecycle.question: Has any email left the system?
lifecycle.cap_stopped: Some went out, then someone pressed Stop
lifecycle.cap_no_recipient: No email went out — resolved to 0 people
lifecycle.cap_failed: No email went out, and that is a failure

detail.title: Send details
detail.nothingToCorrect: No email has gone out — nothing to correct.
detail.cancelBody: No email has left the system. It can be cancelled cleanly.
detail.stopBody: Sent {sent}/{total}. What already went out cannot be recalled — only the rest is stopped.

snapshot.intro: The recipient snapshot is stored with the reason each binding matched. Three months later you can still answer "why did this person get that message".

payload.acceptedTitle: <mono>202</mono> means ACCEPTED, not DELIVERED TO THE INBOX.
payload.duplicate: Duplicate <mono>Idempotency-Key {key}</mono> — the old record is returned, nothing is sent twice. <mono>200</mono> instead of <mono>202</mono>.
payload.collapsed: Collapsed {count} flaps within a 5-minute window into 1 notification.
payload.stale: Expanded from a 3-day-old directory snapshot. Still sent, with a warning.

content.sentVersion: Version sent — the opt-out footer is inserted by the system and locked.
content.noTemplate: This send did not use a template.
content.noneBound: The topic has no bound email template
content.noHtml: Quick compose does not accept raw HTML
content.noHtmlBody: This mode is intentionally stricter. Use a template for personalization.
content.sameForAll: Same content for every recipient. Use a template for personalization.

scheduled.unscheduled: Unscheduled — the draft is reopened for editing
scheduled.author: scheduled by
scheduled.reresolve: Recipients are resolved again from scratch at run time, not taken from the estimate at compose time.
scheduled.dropBody: The send moves to cancelled. The draft is not kept.
scheduled.unscheduleBody: The send goes back to draft; the content is unlocked to edit and schedule again.

compose.title: Compose notification
compose.subtitle: Each draft can be sent only once — check carefully, it cannot be recalled.
compose.runningBody: Current status: {state}. No second send is created.
compose.warning: This email goes out in the name of the organization and cannot be recalled. Recipients are decided by topic + binding; there is no free-form email field.
compose.conflict: Two admins have the same draft open — minh.tran is editing. A later save will not silently overwrite.
compose.conflictDemo: Demo: two admins open the same draft
compose.confirmApproval: This send will create an approval request, not send right away.
compose.confirmNow: Sending now locks the draft and starts the cancel window before the first batch leaves the queue.
compose.zeroBody: Topic {topic} currently resolves to no recipient with an active email channel.
compose.zeroNoChannel: {count} people in {reason} but without an active email channel
compose.zeroOptedOut: {count} people opted out of this topic
compose.zeroNoBinding: The topic has no binding yet.
compose.zeroApiNote: The API path treats 0 recipients as normal (<mono>202</mono> + <mono>no_recipient</mono>). The manual path blocks it — because you would believe it was sent.
compose.forbiddenBody: App Admin can only open topics in the app's namespace.

send.undoTitle: Waiting {seconds} seconds before the first batch leaves the queue.
send.undoBody: Cancel now and nobody receives anything.
send.approvalBody: This send needs Super Admin approval. A request was sent with a preview link of the exact version to be sent.
send.offHours: The email will arrive at <mono>{time}</mono> — outside working hours.
send.scheduledLocked: Content is locked. Recipients are resolved again at run time — people newly in the role receive it, people who just opted out do not.
send.cancelledBody: The send was cancelled. No email left the system. The draft is kept for editing.
send.horizon: The first batch has left the queue
send.queuedNote: No email has left the system. It can be cancelled cleanly.
send.sendingNote: From here nothing can be recalled. Only the unsent part can be stopped.
send.sentNote: Sent {sent}/{total}. Real numbers were fixed at send time.
send.title: Send
send.oncePerDraft: A draft can be sent only once.
send.duplicatedBody: Keeps topic, template and variables — does not copy the old recipient list.
send.savedTemplateBody: Saved in Templates as a draft — a person must preview and Publish it; it is never auto-published.
send.copyNote: The copy keeps topic, template and variables but not the old recipient list.
send.correctionNote: A correction goes only to people who received the original (from the snapshot). Do not confuse people who never got it.
send.noRecall: There is no recall button. Outlook recall only works internally and usually fails once the email is opened.

recipientBlock.optedOut: − {count} people opted out of this topic

recipientBlock.mandatory: Mandatory topic — recipients cannot opt out. This send will need Super Admin approval.

templateEditor.notInApp: This template is not in the app
templateEditor.publishedBody: From the next send on, the app uses this version.
templateEditor.aiBanner: Content drafted by AI, NOT saved. Read it, preview it, then Save draft / Publish yourself — the AI never does either.

aiCompose.title: Ask AI to draft
aiCompose.description: The result is a suggestion — only "Use this version" fills the editor. The AI never saves or publishes on its own.
aiCompose.placeholderNew: e.g. VM overload alert, concise tone, with a metrics table and a Fix now button
aiCompose.placeholderRevise: e.g. shorten to 3 sentences, add an owner line

aiCompose.noVariables: No variables declared — the AI will suggest variables if the email needs them.
aiCompose.sentToProvider: Sent to the AI provider: this description and the names + descriptions of the variables. No sample values, no recipient data.
aiCompose.sentToProviderRevise: Sent to the AI provider: this description, the names + descriptions of the variables, and the current draft. No sample values, no recipient data.
aiCompose.issues: The suggestion has {count} issues — usable, but fix them before Publishing
aiCompose.passes: The suggestion passes the publish checks.
aiCompose.subject: Subject:
aiCompose.suggested: The AI suggests {count} new variables — tick the ones to add to the variable table
aiCompose.suggestedUnchecked: Unticked variables still used in the content must be fixed before Publishing.

templates.title: Templates
templates.subtitle: Admins write and publish · apps send with templateId + payload · always the published version
templates.loadFailed: Could not load the template list
templates.emptyTitle: The app has no templates yet
templates.emptyBody: Create a template, write the content, then Publish — then give the templateId to the app team.
templates.name: Template name
templates.nameHint: Must not match another template in the app — even differing only by case or accents. The ID apps send with is generated by the system.

schema.missingSource: Variables without a source: <mono>{vars}</mono>. Write <mono>'{{ payload.<name> }}'</mono> for data the app sends, or <mono>'{{ user.external_id }}'</mono> for the recipient ID — otherwise it cannot be published.
schema.undeclared: used in the content but not declared
schema.none: No variables yet. Type <mono>'{{ payload.<name> }}'</mono> in the subject or content, then click Declare.
schema.defaultHint: Optional variables need a default written right in the content: <mono>'{{ payload.owner | default: "unknown" }}'</mono>. Values inserted into HTML are always escaped — app data shows up as text, never as HTML tags.

contract.envNote: Template IDs differ between test and production — the app team keeps <mono>templateId</mono> in per-environment configuration. Extra keys in <mono>payload</mono> are ignored.

versions.draftExists: Draft v{version} exists — publish it before creating a draft from another version.
versions.diffBody: Subject + HTML of the two versions side by side.
versions.copyBody: The content and variable table of this version are copied into a new draft. Nothing changes for emails being sent — until you Publish that draft.

previewPane.subject: Subject:
previewPane.hint: Browser preview using sample values. The official check runs at Publish.

editorPane.emptyHint: The editor is empty. Type HTML directly, or ask the AI to draft from a one-line description.
editorPane.jumpTo: Jump to variable '{{' {name} '}}' in the editor

recipients.subtitle: Recipients that {app} has registered through the API. This screen is read-only.

recipientDetail.subtitle: Recipient of {app}, registered at {at}. This screen is read-only.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.subtitle: Subscription = one specific delivery point. This is where messages actually arrive.
subscriptions.emptyBody: Loosen the channel / status / source filters.

import.title: Import CSV
import.subtitle: 3-step dry run — preview first, nothing is written until you confirm
import.rejectedBody: The file lacks the <mono>external_id</mono> column — the whole file is rejected, no row was read.
import.idempotent: Import is idempotent by identity key. Re-running the same file never duplicates users, subscriptions or bindings.
import.auditNote: {count} conflict decisions were audited with your notes.
import.emailOrPhone: Either <mono>email</mono> or <mono>phone</mono> may be empty. If both are empty the row is invalid.
import.tryMissing: Try a file missing a column
import.dryRun: Nothing has been written yet. Click Confirm to write.
import.noAutoMerge: The system never auto-merges conflicts. A person decides, and the decision is audited.

validation.ipRange: IP ranges are not supported yet — enter one address at a time, e.g. 10.20.0.15
validation.ipInvalid: Must be a single IP address, e.g. 10.20.0.15

network.ipHint: The app server IP. One address at a time — ranges are not supported yet.
network.ipEmpty: None declared — EVERY IP can call.
network.loadFailed: Could not read the caller source list
network.title: IP restriction
network.subtitle: IPs allowed to call /v1 and incoming webhooks of {app}
network.limitIpBody: Right now EVERY IP can call. From now on ONLY {value} (and IPs added later) can call — app service servers on other IPs are blocked with IP_NOT_ALLOWED immediately. Check the calling IP before adding.
network.lastIpBody: With no IP in the list, EVERY IP can call — anyone holding the key can call.
network.lastIpExternal: This is an external app: add the new IP FIRST, then remove the old one.
network.lastIpLabel: Remove and open to every IP
network.removeIpBody: App service servers calling from this IP are blocked with IP_NOT_ALLOWED immediately.
network.rules: With no IP listed, every IP can call; once listed, only those IPs get through (both /v1 and incoming webhooks). Each address must match exactly. Changes take effect immediately.
network.externalNoIp: This external app has no IP declared — anyone holding the key can call. Add the app service's server IPs.
network.auditEmpty: No events yet. Audit is written asynchronously, so a just-finished action may not show yet.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.subtitle: API key lifecycle of {app} · app_id never changes
credentials.loadFailed: Could not read the key list
credentials.hashOnly: The system stores only a SHA-256 hash. A lost key cannot be recovered — issue a new one.
credentials.atLimit: There are already {max} active keys — revoke an old key before issuing another.
credentials.emptyBody: {app} has no key yet — the app cannot call /v1. Issue the first key to start.
credentials.auditEmpty: No events yet. Audit is written asynchronously, so a just-finished action may not show yet.
credentials.issueBody: The old key STILL works — issuing does not revoke anything. Move the app service to the new key, then come back and revoke the old one. The new key is shown exactly once.
credentials.revokeBody: Every /v1 call using this key fails immediately. This cannot be undone.

credentialDialog.title: Shown only once
credentialDialog.description: Save app_secret to your secret store before closing.
credentialDialog.appIdNote: <mono>app_id</mono> · Public — fine to embed in the app config
credentialDialog.secretNote: <mono>app_secret</mono> · Secret — the system stores only a hash; the original cannot be shown again
credentialDialog.saved: I have saved app_secret to the secret store
credentialDialog.confirmTitle: Once closed it cannot be recovered. Close anyway?
credentialDialog.confirmBody: You have not copied app_secret. After closing, the system keeps only the hash.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.subtitle: EWS reports delivery results to {app}'s URL
webhooks.notConfiguredTitle: Webhooks are not enabled on the server
webhooks.notConfiguredBody: The EWS server has no webhook signing key (WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY), so URLs cannot be added, secrets rotated or tests sent yet. Contact the EWS operators.
webhooks.intro: Whenever an email has an outcome (sent, failed, blocked), EWS POSTs to the registered URL — the app does not have to keep polling.
webhooks.atLimit: At most {max} URLs per app — delete one before adding another.
webhooks.emptyBody: {app} has not registered for webhooks. Add a URL so EWS reports delivery results.
webhooks.howCall: A POST with a JSON body carrying the event id, event type and the email's outcome. Respond with 2xx within 10 seconds.
webhooks.howSignature: Every call carries <mono>X-EWS-Signature: t=…,v1=…</mono> — verify it with the secret before trusting the body (integration guide, section 5).
webhooks.howRetry: If the app fails or does not answer, EWS retries after 1 min · 5 min · 30 min · 2 h · 6 h, then stops (6 calls in total).
webhooks.howDuplicate: The same event may arrive twice — drop duplicates by <mono>id</mono>.
webhooks.howPrivacy: The body contains no email address and no email content.
webhooks.addBody: The URL must be https:// and reachable from the internet. URLs pointing into a private network are rejected. The secret is shown once right after adding.
webhooks.editBody: Choose which events this URL receives. To change the URL, delete it and add a new one.
webhooks.eventSent: The mail server accepted the email
webhooks.eventFailed: The email could not be sent
webhooks.eventNoRecipient: Not sent because the recipient is blocked (topic off, email unsubscribed…)
webhooks.disableBody: EWS stops calling this URL. Calls waiting for a retry are cancelled — enabling it again does NOT replay old events.
webhooks.rotateBody: The old secret stops working on the NEXT call — the app must switch to the new secret or it will reject every call. The new secret is shown only once.
webhooks.deleteBody: EWS stops calling this URL; pending calls and the call log are deleted. This cannot be undone.
webhooks.secretBody: The secret is shown ONCE. Copy it into the app's configuration — after closing it cannot be shown again, only rotated.
webhooks.secretUsage: The app uses this secret to verify the <mono>X-EWS-Signature</mono> header of every call from EWS.
webhooks.secretSaved: I have stored the secret somewhere safe
webhooks.secretConfirmBody: After closing, this secret cannot be shown again. To get one you will have to rotate it.
webhooks.hintBlocked: The URL points to a private network address — EWS does not call there.
webhooks.hintTimeout: The app did not answer within 10 seconds.
webhooks.hintConnection: Could not connect to the URL (wrong domain, server down, broken HTTPS certificate…).
webhooks.hintHttp: The app answered with a non-2xx code. Check the webhook route and the signature check.
webhooks.hintOther: See the error code next to it.
webhooks.deliveriesEmpty: No calls yet. Send an email, or use Send test.
webhooks.pageSubtitle: Both directions for {app}: EWS reports results to the app, and external tools call in to publish

incoming.notConfigured: Webhooks are not enabled on the server.
incoming.needTopicAndTemplate: Needs an active topic and a published template.
incoming.emptyBody: Add a webhook so another system can send notifications through EWS.
incoming.needsRotation: This URL cannot be recovered — use Rotate URL.
incoming.rotateBody: The old URL stops working immediately.
incoming.deleteBody: The URL stops working immediately. This cannot be undone.
incoming.callDuplicate: Same as before — not sent again
incoming.errInvalidValue: Wrong type (must be text or a number)
incoming.errBody: Body is not a JSON object '{ … }'
incoming.errRateLimited: Too many calls in one minute

systemSettings.title: System settings
systemSettings.subtitle: Operational numbers for every app — no deploy needed
systemSettings.incomingIntro: Applies to every /hooks/… URL of every app.
systemSettings.dedupeHelp: When a call has no dedupe key, identical content within this window publishes only once.
systemSettings.rateHelp: Above this the tool gets 429 — stops an alert storm from sending a flood of emails.
systemSettings.baseUrlHelp: The domain external tools call (through NPM). The console builds full hook URLs from it. Empty = only the /hooks/… part is shown.
systemSettings.outOfRange: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
systemSettings.propagation: New values take effect on every API server within 30 seconds.

quota.title: Channels & Quota
quota.subtitle: Grants by Super Admin and operating limits of {app}
quota.decidedBy: Decided by Super Admin; the App Owner can only propose
quota.allGranted: The app has been granted every channel.
quota.rateLimitNote: Exceeding the rate limit → <mono>429 + Retry-After</mono>; the app is not locked. Only exceeding the volume quota leads to suspension.
quota.requestBody: Super Admin reviews and grants it; the app cannot enable a channel by itself.

profile.title: App profile
profile.subtitle: Registration details of {app}
profile.testSendBody: Simulates the first API call on a new topic.
profile.zeroOk: 0 recipients is expected: a newly created topic has no subscribers yet. This is not an error.

sync.title: Directory sync
sync.subtitle: Latest sync per app — view only
sync.note: Directory sync never deletes opt-out records. People who opted out are still excluded at send time.

allApps.externalTip: The app is outside the internal network — ip_allowlist is required
allApps.title: All apps
allApps.subtitle: Manage publisher registrations and send permissions in EWS Global
allApps.noKeyTitle: Approved {name}, but no key could be issued
allApps.noKeyBody: {message} The app is <mono>active</mono> — go to <link>API keys</link> to issue one.
allApps.emptyBody: No app is in this status.
allApps.loadFailed: Could not read data from the API

approveApp.title: Approve this app?
approveApp.body: Once approved the app can send real email, and the first API key is shown exactly once.
approveApp.confirm: Approve and issue the first key

appTransition.suspendBody: The app stops sending immediately. API keys remain; resuming picks up where it left off — nothing is lost.
appTransition.resumeBody: The app can send again right away. Permissions and API keys stay as they were before suspension.
appTransition.revokeBody: Revoked is a FINAL state — there is no way back, not even resume. The app stops sending permanently. Suspend instead if you might use it again.
appTransition.reasonPlaceholder: The team has ended the project and no longer sends notifications.
appTransition.reasonHint: Required; goes into the system log. Up to 500 characters.

grant.unenforced: These two numbers are currently stored but not enforced — an app over the limit is not rejected. Per-app quota is planned in section 12.5.
grant.ack: This team already has a «Notification settings» screen for employees. Without it, employees have no way to opt out.

wizard.pageSubtitle: Create a new publisher for EWS Notification Service
wizard.profileDraftNote: The app is <mono>active</mono> as soon as it is created and can send email right away — no review.
wizard.namespaceNote: The namespace is the app’s ownership within the organization; only one app per organization holds it. Treat it as fixed once set.
wizard.originNote: <mono>internal</mono> = a service inside the company network. <mono>external</mono> = called from outside.
wizard.grantLater: The sending channel granted by default is email. You get the API key in step 4.
wizard.topicsDraftNote: Topics are created as <mono>draft</mono>; activate them on the Topics screen before sending.
wizard.topicKeyRule: Lowercase letters, digits and <mono>_ . -</mono>, starting with a letter, 2–128 characters.
wizard.topicKeyDuplicate: This key is already used by another topic.
wizard.defaultMode: Default when the user has not chosen
wizard.optIn: opt_in — does NOT receive by default
wizard.mandatoryHint: Users cannot turn it off. Only for messages they must receive, e.g. unusual sign-in alerts — still never sent to broken or unsubscribed addresses.
wizard.reviewNote: Creating registers the app in the system and issues its first API key.
wizard.stoppedTitle: The app was created, but stopped at step «{step}»
wizard.stoppedBody: {message} The app was created and is <mono>active</mono> — do not create it again (the slug would clash); <link>open the app</link> to finish.
wizard.activeNote: The app is active. The new topics are still <mono>draft</mono> — go to <link>Topics</link> and activate them before the app can send.
wizard.orgPlaceholder: Choose the organization that owns this app…
wizard.mandatorySuperAdminOnly: Only a Super Admin can make a topic mandatory — it overrides recipients’ opt-out.
wizard.noOrgBody: Only an organization Owner / Org Admin (or a Super Admin) can register apps. Ask your organization Owner to raise your role.
wizard.create: Create app ({count, plural, one {# topic} other {# topics}})

sendApprovals.title: Send approvals
sendApprovals.subtitle: Sends over the threshold or to mandatory topics.
sendApprovals.auditNote: Approving records in the audit: Composed by <mono>{author}</mono> · Approved by <mono>{reviewer}</mono>
sendApprovals.rejectBody: A reason is required so the author can fix it.

appReview.title: Review app registration
appReview.subtitle: Review the registration request before granting permissions
appReview.decisionNote: Approving issues app_id and app_secret once.
appReview.backToDraft: The registration returns to draft; data is kept.
appReview.rejected: Rejected. The registration returns to <mono>draft</mono>; the App Owner gets the note and can resubmit.
appReview.approved: The registration is approved. The credential was issued once — it will not be shown again.

adjust.ignoredTitle: Channels will be skipped when sending
adjust.ignoredBody: Topic <mono>{topic}</mono> declares channel <mono>{channels}</mono> but the app was not granted it — it will be skipped when sending.

members.appAccessBody: Access of {email} on each app of the organization.
members.noApps: This organization has no apps yet.

members.noPeople: No one to add yet. Ask a Super Admin to make people available in the Directory.

directory.subtitle: EWS accounts of people in the company. Tick someone to make them available when organizations add members. New people from Microsoft 365 start hidden.
